page: Google Cloud Platform c4-highcpu-4 is a compute-optimized virtual machine featuring 4 vCPUs and 8 GB of RAM, yielding a 2.0 GB memory-per-core ratio. Built on the x86_64 architecture, it is powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8581C processor operating at 2.3 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 2 physical cores with 2 threads per core, supported by a 260 MB L3 cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 48 KB L1d cache. This instance does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, and provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data highlights strong single-core performance, with Geekbench single-core and text processing scores reaching top-tier status in the top 10% of tested systems. Single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression also show strong results in the top 25%. However, multi-core and memory-bound operations present clear tradeoffs. Multi-core performance in stress-ng and Passmark CPU tests falls into the bottom 25%, and memory bandwidth benchmarks, such as read-only large block transfers at 38.47 GB/sec and write large block transfers at 25.63 GB/sec, are categorized as weak. Passmark memory scores are poor, placing in the bottom 10%.

Given its resource density and hardware profile, the c4-highcpu-4 offers a specialized cost-efficiency profile suited for compute-heavy tasks that do not require large memory footprints or high memory bandwidth. It is well-suited for single-threaded processing, lightweight web serving, and text processing workloads. It is less optimal for memory-intensive databases, software compilation, or large-scale multi-threaded applications due to its constrained memory capacity and lower multi-core benchmark ratings.
